source_text:
Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐν τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις προσώποις τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ἐθεώρησα ἐν πίστει καὶ ἠγάπησα, παραινῶ, ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ θεοῦ σπουδάζετε πάντα πράσσειν, προκαθημένου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰς τόπον θεοῦ καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων εἰς τόπον συνεδρίου τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ τῶν διακόνων τῶν ἐμοὶ γλυκυτάτων πεπιστευμένων διακονίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δς πρὸ αἰώνων παρὰ πατρὶ ἦν καὶ ἐν τέλει ἐφάνη.
πάντες οὖν ὁμοήθειαν θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐντρέπεσθε ἀλλήλους καὶ μηδεὶς κατὰ σάρκα βλεπέτω τὸν πλησίον, ἀλλ’ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἀλλήλους διὰ παντὸς ἀγαπᾶτε. μηδὲν ἔστω ἐν ὑμῖν, ὃ δυνήσεται ὑμᾶς μερίσαι ἀλλ’ ἑνώθητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τοῖς προκαθημένοις εἰς τύπον καὶ διδαχὴν ἀφθαρσίας.
thought_title: Unity under bishop, elders, and deacons
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Magnesia, urging them to act in unity under their bishop, council of elders, and deacons.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore in the previously written persons the whole multitude I saw in faith and I loved, I urge, in concord of God be eager all things to do, the bishop presiding into place of God and the elders into place of council of the apostles, and the deacons to me most sweet entrusted with service of Jesus Christ, who before ages with the Father was and at the end appeared. All therefore same stamp of God having received respect one another and no one according to flesh let look at the neighbor, but in Jesus Christ one another through all love. Nothing let be among you, which will be able you to divide, but be united to the bishop and to those presiding for type and teaching of incorruption.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive 'of God' as source of the concord, not merely 'godly concord'

choices.term: προκαθημένου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰς τόπον θεοῦ
choices.english: the bishop presiding in the place of God
choices.why: Preserves the spatial metaphor 'into the place of' and the participle's presiding force
rejected: with the bishop in the place of God
the bishop standing in for God

choices.why: Keeps the superlative and the dative of relation

choices.english: having received the same character of God
choices.why: Renders the rare noun literally as 'same character' and keeps the aorist participle

choices.english: for a type and teaching of incorruption
choices.why: Keeps both nouns and the genitive 'of incorruption' governing both
rejected: as a model and lesson of immortality
for an example and instruction in incorruptibility

pass_b_english: Since in the persons I have already named I saw the whole multitude in faith and loved them, I urge you: make it your aim to do everything in the concord of God. Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles, and let the deacons, who are most sweet to me, be entrusted with the service of Jesus Christ, who before the ages was with the Father and appeared at the end.

All of you, then, having taken on God's own character, respect one another, and let no one look at his neighbor according to the flesh, but always love one another in Jesus Christ. Let there be nothing in you that can divide you, but be united with the bishop and with those who preside, as a type and teaching of incorruption.

last_rejected.quote: as a type and teaching of incorruption
last_rejected.why: English omits that the unity with bishop and presiders is 'for/as a type and teaching of incorruption.' The 'as' in English could read as 'in the manner of' rather than 'for the purpose of being.'
last_rejected.fix: be united with the bishop and with those who preside, for a type and teaching of incorruption
last_rejected.ruling: 'as a type and teaching' renders εἰς τύπον καὶ διδαχήν adequately; 'as' conveys purpose/result, no meaning lost.

problems.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

problems.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
problems.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

problems.quote: council of elders of the church
problems.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.

variants.text: council of elders of the church

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'
Same underlying metaphor (charakter/stamp/imprint) rendered differently; reader misses the connection.
problems.fix: Use 'stamp' or 'imprint' consistently for this metaphor.

edits.old: having received the same character of God
edits.new: having received the same stamp of God

fixed: The 'council of elders' and 'council of the apostles' issue is a glossary/consistency concern, not a translation error in this passage; the English already renders the source terms accurately and the typological parallel is clear from 'in the place of'.
The 'council of elders of the church' issue does not appear in this passage.
The 'council of elders' vs 'elders' consistency issue does not appear in this passage.

polish.changed: Clarified the sentence structure by separating the three presiding roles into distinct clauses, so readers can follow who presides, who is entrusted with service, and who appeared at the end. Kept all terms and claims exactly, using the glossary's 'council of elders' consistently.

notes.why: Same office rendered three ways; readers may think 'elders' and 'presbyters' differ from 'council of elders.'
notes.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'council of elders' throughout.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'those who preside' refers to the council of elders, matching the earlier term and removing ambiguity.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.

variants.text: the bishop and the council of elders

notes.why: 'Those who preside' may refer to bishop and elders or to bishops plural; ambiguous.
